title: CLO 2024 Academic Month: Digital Virtual Design Facilitates the Transformation and Upgrade of Fashion Design Education
description: CLO Academic Month 2024 Review! A conversation with Ji Yang, a key faculty member of the Fashion and Apparel Design program at Lian Industrial University’s School of Fashion, sharing how digital apparel technology is integrated into multiple aspects of the teaching system, such as supporting structural teaching, cultivating 3D design thinking, and simulating production processes. Outstanding graduation projects and award-winning competition works were also showcased during the discussion.
transcript:
Good evening, students and teachers online.  
I am Ji Yang, a professional teacher in the field of clothing and apparel at Dalian University.  
Thank you very much for the forum organized by our Colour company.  
I am very happy to be able to share and communicate with you some of my experiences in teaching.  

This time, the topic is **Digital Virtual Design to Help Clothing Design Teaching Transformation and Upgrading**.  
It is mainly divided into three parts.  

The first part is to introduce our professional digitalization development process.  
The second part is to introduce the application and some results of digital virtual design in teaching.  
The third part is to discuss clothing design teaching transformation and upgrade.  

To begin, I would like to talk about the background of our school.  
Our school was established in 1985 as a clothing school.  
It is also the first clothing major in the country.  
In 2013, it became the first comprehensive four-point major in the country.  
There is also a national experimental teaching demonstration center.  
In 2014,  
I received a master’s degree in teaching results.  
In 2015,  
I gained the virtual experimental teaching center in Liaoning Province.  
In 2019,  
we were the first first-class construction major in the country.  

Our school now has four directions:  
- Clothing and apparel design,  
- Clothing design and engineering,  
- Performance,  
- And the digital media technology major that was newly established in 2022.  

Our major focuses on digitalized clothing design teaching.  
It has been developing for nearly 20 years.  

Before 2009,  
digital teaching gradually transformed from traditional teaching to multimedia teaching,  
using digital images such as Photoshop and Kodak,  
software for clothing design and teaching.  

Since 2009,  
our school introduced  
clothing computer-aided design,  
which is the clothing system.  
In this way,  
digital teaching was upgraded.  
At that time,  
the software we cooperated with was AGM, AGM-S.  
When I started teaching,  
it was the first time I came into contact with virtual sewing technology.  
But virtual sewing at that time  
was still very simple.  
It was quite advanced,  
a software that provided a very simple and practical design.  
For example,  
there was a design similar to a clothing model from Sichuan.  
Then it could achieve the effect of virtual sewing and simulation.  

From 2012,  
our school introduced Cloud 3D software.  
At that time,  
it was version 3 or above.  
This version of the software  
was much more mature than what I had seen before.  
Our school had just started using this.  

Regarding digitalization and virtualization, some of the professors and instructors had already started to understand the future of digitalization and virtual clothing design.  
They began research on the digitalization of clothing.  
Some professors and students conducted experiments on clothing engineering, virtual testing, fabric testing, and pressure testing.  

In 2016, some professors and students completed virtualization of their own works.  
At that time, the results were very technological and avant-garde.  
Later, some professors and students started to introduce digital virtualization design into scientific research projects.  

Generally, some professors and students engaged in traditional design,  
some in traditional clothing restoration, sportswear, and some professional clothing.  

In 2016, when the training project was established, our school wanted to apply digitalized virtual technology to the teaching of this course.  

In 2018, the third-year women’s clothing class, the third grade of the 16th batch of students, started the virtual three-dimensional design class.  
At the same time,  
we also used this technology in education reform for structure and engineering, such as digitalization.  

I recall that at that time, the Clo software had reached version 5.0.  
The equipment and computer requirements were very high.  
Previously, our computers could not support it.  
Then our school specially invested a lot of money to build digital virtual computers.  
We also established a digital virtual computer lab to meet the requirements of our teaching and research.  

In 2018, we also passed the preparation for the first batch of virtual  
anti-theft teaching experiments, the national first-class course.  
In the following period, we took several courses in this virtual anti-theft teaching.  
To achieve quality teaching,  
and during the epidemic,  
this kind of digitalized virtual teaching,  
and this virtual anti-theft experimental platform,  
became advantageous.  
This also promoted our digitalization.  
The digitalization of education reform is such a step.  

In 2021, our school began preparing the virtual exhibition of graduates.  
Then in the following year, the college student fashion week was successfully launched in 2022.  
I also participated in some competitions.  
There were also school-level cooperation projects.  

---

**Second part: Application of digital virtual design in education**  

So why do we talk about this virtual design technology  
and introduce it to the fashion design profession?  
In previous guest lectures and other teachers' shares,  
this has been discussed extensively.  
So I will not elaborate much here.  

The main reasons are:  
1. It is the trend for industry development.  
Fashion companies promote the development of the fashion industry, or the green industry.  
In short, the fashion digital virtual design of the fashion industry is undergoing transformation.  
Our school aims to cultivate talents to adapt to the development of this industry.  

2. Virtual design has the potential to improve design efficiency and accuracy.  

3. It strengthens practical control abilities.  

4. It cultivates comprehensive abilities in science and technology departments,  
giving students more design possibilities.  

5. It promotes innovation in teaching methods.  
Because young students prefer this type of virtual digitalization,  
with interactivity and fun,  
this kind of course stimulates students' interest in learning and positivity.  

Mr. Ren shares a lot of such experience in his software courses.  
I teach this type of course as well.  

We have constructed a course system,  
mainly digital virtual design practice.  
Teaching is divided into four parts:  

- The first is the virtual imitation experiment, with a total of five classes.  
In this virtual imitation class,  
students are given questions and virtual imitation tasks to increase interaction.  
It also helps students understand how to transform the structure between three-dimensional and two-dimensional clothing.  

- The second stage is in the third grade.  
We offer digital technology courses, including software for clothing and three-dimensional virtual design.  
In these classes, students operate software in the classroom.  
In large third-grade classes, they start practical homework or major projects.  

- At a higher level, there are practical courses like design internships and comprehensive design,  
all of which can involve virtual design.  
This kind of support is well established, and there is also a lineup of courses.  

This is the application flow I have gone through, and I will share how I use it.  

These two examples open first:  

- The one on the left is the intelligent suit customization,  
which we applied for in 2018.  
- This is mainly a virtual RFI in the field of factory urbanization of Dalian Dayang Fashion Group.  

This class's experimental system is quite large; I took part of it.  
This experiment has a sense of reality,  
allowing students to have magical and practical interaction.  

The experiments are divided into modules such as virtual factory, body shape intelligent evaluation, process preparation, material preparation, cutting, sewing, etc.  

For example, in this virtual simulation experiment,  
we offer courses like clothing equipment cognition and practice, and production management.  
This eliminates the need to take students to visit clothing factories.  
Students can repeatedly study and understand the processes in this virtual simulation.  

There is a complete workflow for suit making,  
including virtual parts, knowledge points, theory, and videos of actual factory operations.  
So even at places like Nanzhuang Tavern,  
this experiment can be used for practical teaching.  

On the right, this is based on the virtual simulation experiment of women's clothing prototype three-dimensional design products.  
This experiment includes modules on women's clothing prototype and body cognition,  
women's clothing prototype virtual structure cognition,  
women's clothing structure and reconstruction,  
and virtual scenario virtual simulation design — four learning modules.  

Currently, this course is mainly for clothing structure and technology,  
and ready-to-wear structure and technology classes.  
Students can learn about clothing structure principles, virtualization, and interactive learning through this course.  
This strengthens students’ understanding of clothing structure and patterns.  

Due to time constraints, I won’t go into more detail.  
Interested students and teachers can visit our official website.  
They can access these two courses on the National Virtual Simulation Experimental Teaching Platform and conduct experimental learning.  

This is three-dimensional virtual stereoscopic design.  
It is a 24-class-hour basic software usage course offered in the third year.  
This is also an introductory course for teacher training.  

It mainly focuses on virtual replacement,  
covering basic styles like shirts, pants, and sweatshirts.  
Through these cases, the course teaches various software operation methods.  
Basic design elements such as color, patterns, fabric design, and adjustment attributes are also covered.  

With this certain level of virtual technology support,  
students learn effectively.  

After mastering this, we also offer the women’s clothing structure design and technology course this semester.  
This course focuses mainly on the theoretical part of innovative structure design.  

Assignments are student-centered,  
with a practical teaching system that inspires and guides students to find current popular clothing images,  
analyze their structural characteristics,  
and then design innovative structures.  

Usually, students work in groups of two to three.  
Based on the theory of innovative structure design,  
students conduct simulated structural design research,  
and then produce samples.  

Previously, students had to repeatedly practice with paper patterns or draping,  
and when problems occurred and the desired effect wasn’t achieved, they had to redo everything,  
which was time-consuming and stressful.  

Since students in the women's clothing direction started learning and attending the Cloud 3D course,  
I encourage them to try using Cloud software for assisted structural design.  

I tell them they can first design the structure according to the style,  
then start with flat or draping patterns,  
then turn the pattern into a digital pattern.  
They can do virtual sewing,  
check for issues in virtual sewing,  
and adjust the pattern in Cloud software.  
Once there are no issues in Cloud and the virtual display is satisfactory,  
they can proceed to make the physical garment,  
and then compare the effects.  

Some students even start entirely with draping,  
then convert the draped pattern into a digital pattern,  
use Cloud for simulation,  
add fabric properties and patterns,  
and compare the results.  

In this process, students strengthen their pattern training,  
improve efficiency,  
and enhance their proficiency in Cloud operation.  

Assignments are done in groups.  
After completing the work, students present PPTs,  
conduct group discussions,  
analyze their simulated designs,  
discuss problems encountered during production,  
and share solutions.  

In recent cohorts, more students use virtual display and virtual fitting.  
Some students even try more interesting experiments.  
Students’ enthusiasm for learning has increased,  
and their practical training and teamwork abilities have been strengthened.  

This is a course continuing from the third year women’s clothing structure design.  
It is a two-week practical course.  

Previously, we collaborated with enterprises for project training.  
Since last year,  
our department head wanted to improve virtual design training.  
So this course was assigned to me.  

In it, students start to enhance their virtual skills.  
Some students still prefer making physical garments first.  

Our college also purchased a PGPMG pattern scanner two years ago.  
At the beginning of this course, we teach how to use the scanner,  
how to scan muslin patterns to digital patterns.  

With digital patterns,  
students start to refine details like fabric texture,  
accessory details, rendering effects, skin of the model,  
and scene setup,  
learning how to operate these in a virtual environment.  

Students can learn flexibly through recorded online courses,  
which helps them master virtual garment sewing technology better.  

They can complete their comprehensive clothing design and innovative structure design.  

For example, this is a conceptual garment inspired by water elements.  
It would be very difficult to make such a piece traditionally,  
but in virtual design,  
students can imagine and practice endlessly.  
Students are quite willing to use virtual design methods for practice.  

At the end of this course, the class presents a two-week practical achievement in a virtual fashion show.  
I have selected parts of it here.  

Among these student works,  
not all reached the level of dynamic runway shows.  
Students also use scenes or post-production methods,  
add motion effects,  
and edit presentations.  
For a structural fashion show,  
the effect is acceptable.  

---

I made a weekly video for them to watch.  
Let's quickly watch it.  

This is a video of a student participating in a skating competition.  
It also includes virtual effects.  

Large garments like this are not very stable.  
It is difficult to achieve a walking effect in a short time.  
So I told the student to record a rotation video.  
Later, we added some movement effects in production.  

This is the creation of the water element at the end.  
I changed it to a more flexible fabric.  

This course is for students.  
It is a fashion design innovation research and practice course.  
It is a general course divided into two stages,  
with a total of 160 class hours.  
It is a second-year course.  

The main courses include a series on new water designers, design planning, creative design, and product practice.  
It also encourages everyone to use virtual design for design assistance.  

Because it is a research subject available nationwide,  
the software used is not only Cloud 3D.  
Many students use other virtual design software.  

When designing, especially conceptual clothing,  
they can better represent design concepts and effects in the virtual environment.  

This student is designing a swimsuit,  
guided by an instructor.  

The entire subject group actually did a fashion show,  
focusing on swimsuits.  
The swimsuit layouts are simple,  
but adjustments are made in the shell software.  
After adjustment, it is mainly for positioning digital printing.  
Within our shell software, digital printing is used again,  
and the effect is particularly good,  
more precise and realistic.  

Next is the graduate design of this department, from 2021.  
Our school prepared for half a year,  
selecting 13 dynamic sets and 26 static sets.  

At that time, the program was still in university.  
We wanted to launch our virtual fashion show at the college student fashion week.  
The theme was “Virtual Coexistence.”  

We attend the college student fashion week every year,  
but due to the epidemic, the school could not display in Beijing for two consecutive years.  
Our school could not reach the Beijing scene,  
so the video of the live show was only recorded in the school auditorium  
and then released at the University of Shenzhen.  

In 2021, because the pandemic was also known as the “year of the universe,”  
the international clothing industry first adopted digitalization to do virtual fashion shows and digital fashion exhibitions.  

So our Dean Ding Wei decided to hold a virtual conference for our graduate students that year.  
At that time, only the women’s direction was open for virtual classes, so we immediately began focusing on real men’s fashion.  
Then the fourth-year students conducted a virtual conference.  

We conducted short-term training,  
and Colov Dpow conducted training for teachers and students at our school.  
This content was emphasized later in our design internship.  

Our teacher organized a graduation event to start clothing and modeling in their own work.  
We chose five or six students to design ten virtual works.  

At that time, we were also working on various digital designs.  
I just wanted to achieve this kind of dynamic show effect.  

Then Mr. Zhang reminded us that if you want to do this kind of large online release,  
you must do it very exquisitely,  
without any errors,  
to reach the level of this release.  

So in the end, we chose 13 dynamic sets,  
and 26 high-definition static sets.  
But the students’ effects were not very perfect.  

I remember Tina Wang Haixia, a technical staff member of Clover,  
helped us with these three sets one by one, changing the original files,  
and then recorded the rendering show.  

Later, Chen Gong helped us synthesize the video.  
At that time, Clover’s team was in Shanghai,  
Dean Ding led our school’s team in Dalian,  
and often held online meetings at night,  
discussing video arrangements.  

There was also a video editing program,  
sometimes running past 10 o’clock at night.  

In total, over four months,  
this historic virtual show was completed.  

This college fashion week was the tenth anniversary last year.  
They wanted to hold offline events but had not yet done so.  
It could not be held until July,  
so it was only online.  

I remember the virtual show of our school at that time.  
There were few participants.  

Wearing gloves is still quite uncomfortable.  
I hope to have a different feeling,  
to get rid of this discomfort.  

I dare say,  
you can find it on the Internet if you want to see what she sees.  

In Shenzhen, it is normal to start offline show releases.  
Our school also went to Beijing to participate in this exhibition.  

This time, the theme was called “Activation of Traditional Technology.”  

The promotional film and invitation letter made at that time were all created using this kind of virtual design.  

This time, our professional design teachers guided students to do virtual design and then costume design.  
Post-production was done by our newly established digital technology teachers.  
They use software such as ZBrush, 3ds Max, Blender, and alternate between them.  

In the end, the final result was this kind of post-production video effect.  

At that time, we still...  
wanted to achieve a real-time virtual common show effect on-site.  
We created a background for that.  

This was also done by the digital media teacher,  
and recorded on-site.  
Because the background is brighter on-site,  
the background may be a bit different.  

In this way, we can also see its virtual effect together on-site.  
It looks better and more impressive on-site.  

In this department and among the students,  
we have been involved in a lot of virtual design teaching.  

In these two years, students have participated in many digital-related competitions,  
such as the Dachuan project, the Challenge Cup, and the Future Designer competition.  
They have won many awards.  

Here, I mainly want to say that last year,  
our school organized participation in the first Zeta Cloud Cup,  
China’s original universe clothing design competition.  

Many students were voted for.  
I remember at least 12 students entered three tracks.  
Finally...  
Lai Yuxin won the gold medal in the leisure sports group.  
Chen Lin won an award in the creative suit and play group.  

This is their virtual effect.  

---

**Third part: Clothing design teaching transformation and upgrade**  

When it comes to transformation and upgrade,  
it is about introducing virtual technology,  
including virtual needle testing,  
to improve our teaching quality and effectiveness.  

It also involves increasing the number of teachers.  
Through extensive training,  
and this lecture forum,  
our teachers improve digital education awareness  
and teaching ability.  

Students strengthen their practical education.  
The main goal is to train creative thinking and creativity.  

In course setting,  
training programs are adjusted multiple times  
according to industry needs and development trends.  

For example,  
some teachers are also participating in the new 2024 training program,  
whether for private schools or graduate students.  
Many adjustments have been made.  

For example, our school’s 2024 training program this year  
focuses more on market demand,  
adding a digital fashion design research direction.  
Design is the core,  
integrating art and science,  
facing the new industry,  
the development needs of new technologies and new positions,  
cultivating multi-dimensional, cross-integrated digital talents.  

The development of digital design  
in our entire education upgrade,  
I think can be divided into three parts:  

1. The combination of design and technology.  
Currently, through digital virtual design,  
three-dimensional modeling,  
virtual reality, and other technologies,  
we create a flexible design environment for students.  

2. We are now studying the integration of technology and digital virtual design,  
promoting the deep integration of design and technology.  

For example, 3D printing,  
intelligent wear,  
ergonomics,  
and cooperation models like these  
not only broaden the boundaries of design,  
but also provide more inspiration sources for designers.  

3. The collision of design and intelligence.  
Intelligence, intellectualization,  
and artificial intelligence are topics we cannot avoid.  

Artificial intelligence,  
big data,  
Internet of Things,  
etc.,  
bring new possibilities to clothing design.  

Intelligent technology  
can help designers improve design efficiency and quality,  
realize intelligent and automated design.  

We should not fear artificial intelligence.  
In fact,  
I think we can use artificial intelligence well,  
just like we use virtual technology well.  

This can integrate artificial intelligence into our virtual technology,  
and into our design teaching,  
to upgrade clothing design to a higher level of transformation.  

Finally, let me show our school’s two exhibitions with the theme:  
**Virtual Coalescence, Activate the Future**.  

This concludes my share today.  
Thank you all.

chunks.content: # Digital Virtual Design Facilitates the Transformation and Upgrade of Fashion Design Education This document presents an in-depth overview of the integration of digital virtual design technologies in fashion design education, highlighting the development process, practical applications, and strategic transformation of teaching methods. It includes technical details on software, virtual simulation experiments, course structures, and industry collaboration to support the digital upgrade of fashion education. --- ## 1. Development of Digital Virtual Design in Fashion Education This section outlines the historical and technical progression of digital virtual design at Dalian University’s clothing and apparel department, emphasizing milestones in software adoption, experimental teaching platforms, and digital infrastructure development. ### Institutional Background and Digitalization Milestones - Dalian University’s clothing school was established in 1985 as China's first clothing major. - It became the first comprehensive four-point major in 2013 and has a national experimental teaching demonstration center. - Key recognitions: - Master’s degree in teaching results (2014). - Virtual experimental teaching center in Liaoning Province (2015). - First-class construction major status (2019). - Current academic directions include: - Clothing and apparel design - Clothing design and engineering - Performance arts related to clothing - Digital media technology (established in 2022) ### Evolution of Digital Teaching (2000–Present) - **Pre-2009:** Transition from traditional to multimedia teaching using tools like Photoshop and Kodak for clothing design. - **2009:** Introduction of clothing computer-aided design (CAD) systems, partnering with software such as AGM and AGM-S; early use of virtual sewing technology which was simple but practical. - **2012:** Adoption of Cloud 3D software (version 3+), marking a significant upgrade in digital virtualization capabilities. - Early research on digital clothing included virtual testing, fabric testing, pressure testing, and engineering experiments. ### Virtualization Integration and Infrastructure - By 2016, virtualization of designs by professors and students became technologically advanced and avant-garde. - Digital virtualization design was integrated into scientific research projects. - The 2016 training project aimed to apply digital virtual technology in teaching courses. - In 2018, the third-year women’s clothing class began virtual 3D design courses. - Clo software version 5.0 required high computer specifications, prompting investment in a dedicated digital virtual computer lab. - The national first-class virtual anti-theft experimental platform was prepared in 2018, significantly aiding digital education reform. - During the COVID-19 pandemic, virtual experimental platforms allowed uninterrupted quality teaching. - By 2021–2022, initiatives included virtual exhibitions and launching the college student fashion week with virtual design participation. --- ## 2. Application of Digital Virtual Design in Fashion Design Education This section discusses practical applications, course structures, and examples of digital virtual design technologies in fashion education, focusing on software usage, experimental modules, and student projects. ### Rationale for Integrating Virtual Design - Aligns with industry trends towards green and digital fashion development. - Enhances design efficiency, accuracy, and practical control. - Cultivates interdisciplinary skills combining science and technology. - Encourages innovative, interactive, and engaging teaching approaches favored by younger students.

chunks.content: Application of Digital Virtual Design in Fashion Design Education This section discusses practical applications, course structures, and examples of digital virtual design technologies in fashion education, focusing on software usage, experimental modules, and student projects. ### Rationale for Integrating Virtual Design - Aligns with industry trends towards green and digital fashion development. - Enhances design efficiency, accuracy, and practical control. - Cultivates interdisciplinary skills combining science and technology. - Encourages innovative, interactive, and engaging teaching approaches favored by younger students. ### Course System and Teaching Approach The digital virtual design curriculum is divided into four progressive stages: 1. **Virtual Imitation Experiment (Five classes):** Students engage in virtual imitation tasks to understand the transformation between 2D and 3D clothing structures through interactive assignments. 2. **Digital Technology Courses (Third Year):** Includes software training in clothing design and 3D virtual design, with practical homework and major projects to apply learned skills. 3. **Advanced Practical Courses:** Design internships and comprehensive design courses incorporate virtual design techniques, supported by an established course lineup. ### Virtual Simulation Experiments - **Intelligent Suit Customization (2018):** Collaboration with Dalian Dayang Fashion Group for virtual RFI in factory urbanization. Modules include virtual factory simulation, body shape evaluation, process and material preparation, cutting, and sewing. The simulation enables students to understand factory production workflows without physical visits, using video and theoretical materials. - **Women’s Clothing Prototype 3D Design:** Four modules cover body cognition, virtual structure cognition, reconstruction, and virtual scenario simulation. Used primarily in clothing structure and technology courses, this enhances understanding of garment patterns and structures. ### Software and Practical Training - **Basic 3D Virtual Design Course:** A 24-class-hour course focusing on virtual replacement of standard garments (shirts, pants, sweatshirts). Covers software operations and design elements like color, patterns, fabric design, and adjustments. - **Women’s Clothing Structure Design and Technology:** Theoretical course encouraging innovative structural design based on popular clothing images, with group assignments involving simulated research and sample production. - **Cloud 3D Software Integration:** Students design virtual garments by creating digital patterns, performing virtual sewing, and adjusting designs before physical production. This reduces errors and enhances efficiency compared to traditional pattern making and draping. - **PGPMG Pattern Scanner Usage:** Introduced two years ago to digitize muslin patterns for virtual refinement, including fabric texture, accessories, rendering, and scene setup. - **Virtual Fashion Show:** Culminates in a two-week practical course where students present virtual garments in dynamic or post-production simulated runway shows, integrating motion and effects. ### Expanded Use of Virtual Design Software - Beyond Cloud 3D, students use other platforms for conceptual designs. - Example projects include swimsuit design with digital printing adjustments via Shell software, enhancing precision and realism. ### Graduate Virtual Fashion Shows (2021) - Preparation involved selecting 13 dynamic sets and 26 static sets for a virtual fashion show themed “Virtual Coexistence.” - Due to COVID-19, shows were recorded on campus and broadcast remotely. - The project involved extensive collaboration between university teams and Clover’s technical staff for file optimization, rendering, and video synthesis.

chunks.content: ### Expanded Use of Virtual Design Software - Beyond Cloud 3D, students use other platforms for conceptual designs. - Example projects include swimsuit design with digital printing adjustments via Shell software, enhancing precision and realism. ### Graduate Virtual Fashion Shows (2021) - Preparation involved selecting 13 dynamic sets and 26 static sets for a virtual fashion show themed “Virtual Coexistence.” - Due to COVID-19, shows were recorded on campus and broadcast remotely. - The project involved extensive collaboration between university teams and Clover’s technical staff for file optimization, rendering, and video synthesis. - The show took over four months to complete, marking a milestone in digital fashion education. ### Industry Collaboration and Competitions - Students participated in competitions like the Dachuan project, Challenge Cup, Future Designer competition, and the first Zeta Cloud Cup. - Achievements include a gold medal in the leisure sports group and awards in creative suit design. --- ## 3. Transformation and Upgrade of Clothing Design Teaching This section covers strategic changes in curriculum, faculty development, and integration of emerging technologies such as AI to advance fashion design education. ### Goals and Strategies for Transformation - Incorporate virtual technologies including virtual needle testing to elevate teaching quality. - Expand faculty capabilities through extensive training and forums to enhance digital education awareness. - Strengthen students’ practical and creative skills. ### Curriculum Adjustments - Training programs are continuously updated to match industry needs, including the 2024 program focusing on market demand. - New research directions emphasize digital fashion design integrating art and science. - Aim to cultivate multi-dimensional, cross-disciplinary digital talents. ### Three Pillars of Digital Design Development 1. **Integration of Design and Technology:** Utilizing 3D modeling, virtual reality, and related technologies to create flexible design environments. 2. **Deep Integration of Digital Virtual Design and Technology:** Exploring applications like 3D printing, intelligent wearables, and ergonomics to expand design boundaries and inspire innovation. 3. **Collision of Design and Intelligence:** Embracing artificial intelligence (AI), big data, and Internet of Things (IoT) to improve design efficiency, quality, and automation. ### Artificial Intelligence in Fashion Design Education - AI is viewed as an enabler rather than a threat. - Integration of AI with virtual technology can elevate clothing design teaching and innovation. - Encourages proactive use of AI tools alongside virtual design platforms. ### Showcase Exhibitions - The school hosted exhibitions themed **“Virtual Coalescence, Activate the Future.”** - Events included virtual design-guided costume creation, post-production using software like ZBrush, 3ds Max, and Blender. - Combined on-site recordings with virtual backgrounds to enhance presentation effects. ### Student Achievements and Industry Exposure - Students have actively participated in digital design competitions and won multiple awards. - The school’s engagement with digital virtual design has fostered collaboration, innovation, and recognition in the fashion education community. --- # Summary Dalian University’s clothing and apparel program has pioneered the integration of digital virtual design into fashion education through a structured progression of software adoption, experimental teaching, and curriculum innovation.

markdown_content: # Digital Virtual Design Facilitates the Transformation and Upgrade of Fashion Design Education This document presents an in-depth overview of the integration of digital virtual design technologies in fashion design education, highlighting the development process, practical applications, and strategic transformation of teaching methods. It includes technical details on software, virtual simulation experiments, course structures, and industry collaboration to support the digital upgrade of fashion education. --- ## 1. Development of Digital Virtual Design in Fashion Education This section outlines the historical and technical progression of digital virtual design at Dalian University’s clothing and apparel department, emphasizing milestones in software adoption, experimental teaching platforms, and digital infrastructure development. ### Institutional Background and Digitalization Milestones - Dalian University’s clothing school was established in 1985 as China's first clothing major. - It became the first comprehensive four-point major in 2013 and has a national experimental teaching demonstration center. - Key recognitions: - Master’s degree in teaching results (2014). - Virtual experimental teaching center in Liaoning Province (2015). - First-class construction major status (2019). - Current academic directions include: - Clothing and apparel design - Clothing design and engineering - Performance arts related to clothing - Digital media technology (established in 2022) ### Evolution of Digital Teaching (2000–Present) - **Pre-2009:** Transition from traditional to multimedia teaching using tools like Photoshop and Kodak for clothing design. - **2009:** Introduction of clothing computer-aided design (CAD) systems, partnering with software such as AGM and AGM-S; early use of virtual sewing technology which was simple but practical. - **2012:** Adoption of Cloud 3D software (version 3+), marking a significant upgrade in digital virtualization capabilities. - Early research on digital clothing included virtual testing, fabric testing, pressure testing, and engineering experiments. ### Virtualization Integration and Infrastructure - By 2016, virtualization of designs by professors and students became technologically advanced and avant-garde. - Digital virtualization design was integrated into scientific research projects. - The 2016 training project aimed to apply digital virtual technology in teaching courses. - In 2018, the third-year women’s clothing class began virtual 3D design courses. - Clo software version 5.0 required high computer specifications, prompting investment in a dedicated digital virtual computer lab. - The national first-class virtual anti-theft experimental platform was prepared in 2018, significantly aiding digital education reform. - During the COVID-19 pandemic, virtual experimental platforms allowed uninterrupted quality teaching. - By 2021–2022, initiatives included virtual exhibitions and launching the college student fashion week with virtual design participation. --- ## 2. Application of Digital Virtual Design in Fashion Design Education This section discusses practical applications, course structures, and examples of digital virtual design technologies in fashion education, focusing on software usage, experimental modules, and student projects. ### Rationale for Integrating Virtual Design - Aligns with industry trends towards green and digital fashion development. - Enhances design efficiency, accuracy, and practical control. - Cultivates interdisciplinary skills combining science and technology. - Encourages innovative, interactive, and engaging teaching approaches favored by younger students. ### Course System and Teaching Approach The digital virtual design curriculum is divided into four progressive stages: 1. **Virtual Imitation Experiment (Five classes):** Students engage in virtual imitation tasks to understand the transformation between 2D and 3D clothing structures through interactive assignments. 2. **Digital Technology Courses (Third Year):** Includes software training in clothing design and 3D virtual design, with practical homework and major projects to apply learned skills. 3. **Advanced Practical Courses:** Design internships and comprehensive design courses incorporate virtual design techniques, supported by an established course lineup. ### Virtual Simulation Experiments - **Intelligent Suit Customization (2018):** Collaboration with Dalian Dayang Fashion Group for virtual RFI in factory urbanization. Modules include virtual factory simulation, body shape evaluation, process and material preparation, cutting, and sewing. The simulation enables students to understand factory production workflows without physical visits, using video and theoretical materials. - **Women’s Clothing Prototype 3D Design:** Four modules cover body cognition, virtual structure cognition, reconstruction, and virtual scenario simulation. Used primarily in clothing structure and technology courses, this enhances understanding of garment patterns and structures. ### Software and Practical Training - **Basic 3D Virtual Design Course:** A 24-class-hour course focusing on virtual replacement of standard garments (shirts, pants, sweatshirts). Covers software operations and design elements like color, patterns, fabric design, and adjustments. - **Women’s Clothing Structure Design and Technology:** Theoretical course encouraging innovative structural design based on popular clothing images, with group assignments involving simulated research and sample production. - **Cloud 3D Software Integration:** Students design virtual garments by creating digital patterns, performing virtual sewing, and adjusting designs before physical production. This reduces errors and enhances efficiency compared to traditional pattern making and draping. - **PGPMG Pattern Scanner Usage:** Introduced two years ago to digitize muslin patterns for virtual refinement, including fabric texture, accessories, rendering, and scene setup. - **Virtual Fashion Show:** Culminates in a two-week practical course where students present virtual garments in dynamic or post-production simulated runway shows, integrating motion and effects. ### Expanded Use of Virtual Design Software - Beyond Cloud 3D, students use other platforms for conceptual designs. - Example projects include swimsuit design with digital printing adjustments via Shell software, enhancing precision and realism. ### Graduate Virtual Fashion Shows (2021) - Preparation involved selecting 13 dynamic sets and 26 static sets for a virtual fashion show themed “Virtual Coexistence.” - Due to COVID-19, shows were recorded on campus and broadcast remotely. - The project involved extensive collaboration between university teams and Clover’s technical staff for file optimization, rendering, and video synthesis. - The show took over four months to complete, marking a milestone in digital fashion education. ### Industry Collaboration and Competitions - Students participated in competitions like the Dachuan project, Challenge Cup, Future Designer competition, and the first Zeta Cloud Cup. - Achievements include a gold medal in the leisure sports group and awards in creative suit design. --- ## 3. Transformation and Upgrade of Clothing Design Teaching This section covers strategic changes in curriculum, faculty development, and integration of emerging technologies such as AI to advance fashion design education. ### Goals and Strategies for Transformation - Incorporate virtual technologies including virtual needle testing to elevate teaching quality. - Expand faculty capabilities through extensive training and forums to enhance digital education awareness. - Strengthen students’ practical and creative skills. ### Curriculum Adjustments - Training programs are continuously updated to match industry needs, including the 2024 program focusing on market demand. - New research directions emphasize digital fashion design integrating art and science. - Aim to cultivate multi-dimensional, cross-disciplinary digital talents. ### Three Pillars of Digital Design Development 1. **Integration of Design and Technology:** Utilizing 3D modeling, virtual reality, and related technologies to create flexible design environments. 2. **Deep Integration of Digital Virtual Design and Technology:** Exploring applications like 3D printing, intelligent wearables, and ergonomics to expand design boundaries and inspire innovation. 3. **Collision of Design and Intelligence:** Embracing artificial intelligence (AI), big data, and Internet of Things (IoT) to improve design efficiency, quality, and automation. ### Artificial Intelligence in Fashion Design Education - AI is viewed as an enabler rather than a threat. - Integration of AI with virtual technology can elevate clothing design teaching and innovation. - Encourages proactive use of AI tools alongside virtual design platforms. ### Showcase Exhibitions - The school hosted exhibitions themed **“Virtual Coalescence, Activate the Future.”** - Events included virtual design-guided costume creation, post-production using software like ZBrush, 3ds Max, and Blender. - Combined on-site recordings with virtual backgrounds to enhance presentation effects. ### Student Achievements and Industry Exposure - Students have actively participated in digital design competitions and won multiple awards. - The school’s engagement with digital virtual design has fostered collaboration, innovation, and recognition in the fashion education community. --- # Summary Dalian University’s clothing and apparel program has pioneered the integration of digital virtual design into fashion education through a structured progression of software adoption, experimental teaching, and curriculum innovation. Practical applications include virtual factory simulations, 3D garment design, advanced digital pattern making, and virtual fashion shows. The program emphasizes the fusion of design, technology, and intelligence, preparing students for the evolving digital fashion industry. Continuous upgrades in faculty skills, course content, and technology adoption aim to transform traditional fashion education into a multi-dimensional, interactive, and AI-augmented learning environment.
